claims.text: Premelting and melting in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles are primarily governed by temperature-induced copper surface segregation.
Heating causes copper atoms to migrate preferentially toward nanoparticle surfaces.
Surface-segregated copper forms a copper-rich shell.
The copper-rich shell becomes liquid-like before the alloy core melts.
The starting equiatomic Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles have a statistically homogeneous elemental distribution.
An ultrathin inert coating can inhibit copper surface segregation by impeding surface diffusion.
Copper has a lower melting point than the other constituents of the proposed Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu alloy.
Copper has sufficiently lower surface energy than the other constituents to drive its segregation to the nanoparticle surface.
Copper migration to the surface is thermally activated.
Copper segregation lowers the effective melting temperature of the nanoparticle surface.
Melting begins at the surface and propagates inward as temperature increases.
Uncoated baseline nanoparticles will begin surface premelting at a lower temperature than coated nanoparticles in which copper segregation is suppressed.
Suppressing copper segregation will delay surface melting.
When copper segregation is suppressed, the overall melting transition will more closely resemble that of a chemically homogeneous particle.
Surface effects are dominant for the proposed nanoparticles at diameters typically below 10 nm.
The mechanism is expected to apply to high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles containing a constituent with substantially lower melting point and surface energy than the other constituents.
Particle size, interfacial energies, and kinetic factors may affect the premelting-temperature offset and extent of copper enrichment.
Failure to observe a copper-rich, liquid-like surface before full melting would falsify the proposed segregation-controlled mechanism.
Failure of segregation-inhibiting coated particles to show a higher premelting onset than baseline particles would falsify the proposed mechanism.
